Innora Security Research · ai0day.com · Continuous vulnerability research & exploitability analysis
This repository publishes Innora's ongoing security research: root-cause analysis, reproduction environments, exploitability primitives, and mitigation guidance for vulnerabilities we investigate — primarily Linux kernel networking bugs and related infrastructure.
Each CVE gets its own directory containing:
Root-cause analysis — the exact code path, race window, and lifetime bug
Reproduction environment — QEMU-based, self-contained, no external targets
Exploitability primitives — what an attacker can realistically build
Patch matrix & defense guidance — fixed versions and detection/mitigation
Our research pipeline (the ai0day pipeline ):
Triage — CVE analysis, affected-version mapping, exploitability scoring
Reproduction — deterministic trigger engineering (KASAN-verified)
Primitive extraction — heap layout, TOCTOU, OOB read/write analysis
Chain validation — end-to-end exploit primitive verification
Disclosure — coordinated with upstream fix availability
Our primary purpose is cybersecurity research. We publish research technical details only — a complete weaponized exploit will not be made public in the short term, as releasing one would be publishing a network weapon, which we consider irresponsible.
All research targets already-patched vulnerabilities (upstream fix released before or alongside our publication)
Reproduction environments are self-contained (QEMU VMs, custom-built kernels) — nothing here runs against live systems
See POLICY.md for our full publication policy
